title: Canada seeking interim trade arrangement with U.S. by end of year: sources

image.caption: Canada-U.S. Trade Minister Dominic LeBlanc met with advisory committee members on Thursday about the state of negotiations with the Trump administration. (Justin Tang/The Canadian Press)

blocks.text: Canada is seeking to reach an interim tariff arrangement with the Trump administration by the end of the year, rather than a full trade deal, sources tell CBC News.
Negotiators seeking relief on steel, aluminum, auto, lumber and other sectors
· Posted: Nov 19, 2026 2:04 PM EST | Last Updated: 18 minutes ago
Canada-U.S. Trade Minister Dominic LeBlanc met with the federal government's Canada-U.S economic advisory committee on Thursday.

Sources with knowledge of the meeting said that the government's goal to reach an interim agreement, rather than a permanent new deal, would cover Section 232 tariffs on steel, aluminum, auto and lumber — as well as Section 338 tariffs imposed on Canadian goods in August after previous talks broke down.
Prime Minister Mark Carney is heading back to Ottawa after a nine-day trade mission to Europe and Asia.

items: 'If the U.S. doesn't want to do a deal, we're busy,' Carney says
Canada's trade with China isn't U.S. president's top concern: Carney

blocks.text: Speaking virtually to the Dealbook summit from China on Wednesday, Carney said Canada continues "to have a series of issues" when it comes to trade with the U.S.
The prime minister indicated that there had been progress toward an agreement in recent weeks but said they're not at the point of putting anything to paper.

Carney met with U.S. President Donald Trump in China on the sidelines of the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) summit — a conversation he described as "reasonably direct" but one that didn't produce a trade breakthrough.

During his latest trip, Carney brokered free trade deals with the Philippines and the 11-nation ASEAN bloc — and secured meaningful market access for Canadian commodities in return for allowing a relatively small number of Chinese EVs to be imported at lower tariff rates and adjustments to import rules for certain Chinese steel and aluminum products.
"We'd like to do a deal. If the U.S. doesn't want to do a deal, we're busy," Carney told the summit's audience in New York.

Darren Major is a senior writer for CBC's parliamentary bureau in Ottawa. He previously worked as a digital reporter for CBC Ottawa and a producer for CBC's Power & Politics.
